newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish grain prices set to rise as output falls.
newsitem.headline: Spanish grain prices set to rise as output falls.

text.p: Spanish cereal prices are expected to soar in coming months as a lack of rain reduces the harvest, traders said on Monday.
Recent rainfall raised hopes of softer prices but in fact left the market little changed.
"We'll end the year with prices higher than now," a Madrid-based dealer said.

"Rain after all was very limited. The only prices which are really falling are foreign ones. A drought in Spain is very tough, more dangerous than in the Northern countries because we've got the hottest weather," he added.
Ex-farm milling wheat was trading at around 28,000 pesetas per tonne on Monday, unchanged since April 18, while imported milling wheat eased to around 26,000 from 27,000.
"Rain didn't change prospects that much," a trader in Barcelona said, "and what is playing against us is also the fact that foreign prices have been sustained."
Some farmers have been hoarding crops in anticipation of higher prices.
"Farmers are saying for example that barley is trading at around 24,000 per tonne, but it's really hard to find somebody who really wants to sell barley at that price," a dealer added.
Estimates for 1997 predict a drop of 15 to 30 percent in output from last year's crop of around 20 million tonnes.
The only exception was thought to be maize, with the crop seen increasing slightly this year and prices expected to ease a little as a consequence.
Dealers said the lack of rain was hurting the southern regions most, where hard wheat is mainly produced and soft wheat production is limited.
